name: Schloss Ambras
kurzbeschreibung: Renaissance castle Ambras overlooking Innsbruck houses the world's oldest preserved museum collection and the magnificent Spanish Hall.
beschreibung:
Overview

The magnificent Schloss Ambras perches high on a forested hillside southeast of Tyrol's capital, Innsbruck. It is inextricably linked to Archduke Ferdinand II (1529–1595), who converted the medieval fortress into an opulent Renaissance palace for his morganatic wife Philippine Welser. A devoted collector and humanist, Ferdinand established the world's very first purpose-built museum complex here. Today, Schloss Ambras belongs to the Kunsthistorisches Museum Vienna and showcases internationally acclaimed collections, including historic armouries, the celebrated Chamber of Art and Curiosities, and the Habsburg Portrait Gallery.

Route & Requirements

The museum trail encompasses the Lower Castle and Upper Castle. The Lower Castle contains the imperial Armouries, displaying ornate tournament armour, and the famed Chamber of Art and Curiosities, packed with scientific instruments, coral carvings, and exotic natural specimens. Connecting the wings is the monumental 43-metre-long Spanish Hall, one of the finest freestanding Renaissance halls in existence. The Upper Castle displays more than 200 royal portraits by Titian, Van Dyck, and Velázquez. Surrounding the palace, a romantic landscaped English park with scenic ponds invites leisurely walking. The Upper Castle is fully wheelchair-accessible via elevators, and park walkways are well surfaced.

Visit & Arrival

Schloss Ambras is open daily from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed for maintenance in November; the castle park remains open and free of charge year-round). Standard museum admission is roughly 16.00 Euro for adults; visitors under 19 enjoy free entry. From Innsbruck Main Station, take tram line 3 to the Ambras stop (a 10-minute walk) or board the Innsbruck Sightseer bus directly to the castle gates. By car, take the A12/A13 motorways to the Innsbruck-Ost or Innsbruck-Mitte exits; paid visitor parking is available on site.

Tips

Attending a classical chamber concert in the Spanish Hall during the Innsbruck Festival of Early Music is unforgettable. Don't miss exploring the Bacchus Grotto and waterfall paths in the castle park for scenic valley vistas.
